sentences.text: The only known fossils of Zhyraornis consist of partial pelvic bones known as synsacra, which are fused vertebrae supporting the tail.
Fossils of Zhyraornis were discovered in the Bissekty Formation near Dzharakuduk in the Kyzyl Kum desert of Uzbekistan.
Paleontologist Lev Nesov originally classified Zhyraornis in the family Zhyraornithidae and the suborder Zhyraornithi within the order Ichthyornithiformes.
In 1996, Kurochkin reclassified Zhyraornis as a member of the family Alexornithidae within the Enantiornithes.
In 2006, Kurochkin reclassified Zhyraornis as a primitive member of the Ornithuromorpha, the lineage leading to modern birds.
The exact evolutionary relationships of Zhyraornis remain unresolved among scientists.
Zhyraornis lived during the late Cretaceous period, specifically the middle Turonian stage, approximately 92 million years ago.
The time range for Zhyraornis spans from the Cenomanian to the Turonian, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
